decisions.I1-sanitization-stance: KEEP the documented stance (transparent-ish proxy: neutralize C0/C1/DEL/bidi/zero-width control chars in LLM-visible display annotations only; pass natural-language description text, schema validation strings (enum/const/default/pattern), and invoke_tool arg+result bytes through verbatim per D-004; injection defense lives at the inference layer). NO natural-language scrubbing, NO untrusted-content envelope. User-confirmed. Action is test+doc LOCK only, no behavior change.
decisions.I2-truncation-fix: The ~100-char cap is a list_tools-row summary control ONLY (documented in SECURITY.md + GOTCHA #20). It currently LEAKS into get_tool_schema annotation strings via the shared sanitize_upstream_text (server.rs:369), silently truncating real argument docs mid-word. FIX: decouple control-neutralization (applies to both list_tools rows AND get_tool_schema annotations) from length-capping (list_tools rows ONLY). get_tool_schema annotations stay control-neutralized + single-line but FULL-LENGTH. Orchestrator-driven; aligns code to documented intent.
decisions.I2-test-contract-conflict: tests/integration/sanitization.rs lines ~411-446 (get_tool_schema_sanitizes_poisoned_metadata_preserves_shape) and ~946-968 (F3 annotation block) currently ASSERT get_tool_schema title/description/$comment are <= DESC_CAP(120). Those assertions LOCK the Issue-2 bug. test-creator (sole test authority) must FLIP them to assert FULL pass-through (no cap), keeping the control-free + single-line assertions. list_tools-row cap assertions stay unchanged.

ISSUE 1 (HIGH, sanitization stance) — validated as ALREADY-DECIDED design (D-004 + SECURITY.md + GOTCHA #20); user locked the keep-stance option; action = regression-test the contract (invoke control-char round-trip) + sharpen SECURITY.md. ISSUE 2 (MEDIUM, silent ~100-char truncation in get_tool_schema) — validated as a GENUINE bug: the list-row cap leaks into the schema-detail fidelity path; fix = decouple cap from control-strip; requires flipping existing test assertions.
